gaps.sentence: You should get that rash ___ (look at) by a doctor.
gaps.explanation: Causative 'get something done': get + object + past participle (looked at).

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
gaps.explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

gaps.sentence: The road ___ at the moment — use the bypass.
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' — present continuous passive: is being repaired.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of homes ___ (flood) when the river burst its banks.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + flooded. The cause (the river) is in the when-clause.

gaps.sentence: The whole street ___ when the gas main burst.
gaps.explanation: The street was evacuated by others: past necessity had to be + evacuated.

gaps.sentence: The report must ___ before Friday's board meeting.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: must be + submitted. 'Been' would require have (must have been submitted).

gaps.sentence: The company ___ (say) to be on the verge of bankruptcy.
gaps.explanation: It is said that... → The company is said to be... Present simple passive: is said.
